role: Preregistered contract for the v0.6 The Well shear_flow inverse. It recovers viscosity nu and tracer diffusivity kappa from sparse probes of a named public subset. It holds no v0.6 test number. It does not edit v0.5.2 or earlier artifacts.
question: On a documented subset of The Well shear_flow, can a solver-free weak-form coefficient fit, a data-only FNO inverse, and an FNO-bracket hybrid with split-conformal intervals recover nu = 1/Re and kappa = 1/(Re Sc) from sparse noisy probes, against the frozen roadmap bars?

attribution.generator: Dedalus (Burns et al., Phys. Rev. Research 2, 023068, 2020)
attribution.access: huggingface_hub anonymous; no token. If rate-limited, back off and record the failure. Do not request credentials.

not_claimed: that a Dedalus or other PDE solver was run on these fields
a retuned bar after seeing test scores
a change to any v0.5.2, v0.5.1, v0.5, v0.4.1, or v0.4 number, protocol, or score file

aggregation.unit: one (nu, kappa) pair per instance per method per noise, then median relative error over the slice
aggregation.center: median over instances, then mean over seeds
aggregation.coverage: fraction of test instances whose true nu and true kappa both lie in their 0.9 split-conformal intervals

pde.form: u_t + u·∇u + ∇p = nu Δu;  s_t + u·∇s = kappa Δs;  periodic;  mean(p) = 0

source_grid.note: Official The Well page. Axis order is read from each HDF5 dimensions group.

downsample.method: periodic Fourier truncation: keep the lowest nx_coarse/2 and ny_coarse/2 modes on each axis, scale by (n_coarse/n_fine), inverse FFT. That is the anti-aliasing. No spatial window.

time_window.note: Frames are indices into the 200 stored steps. The window is mid-run after the initial shear transient.

sensors.layout: equispaced lattice, stride 4 on the 32 by 64 coarse grid

noise.model: additive iid Gaussian on observed field values, scaled by the clean-field standard deviation of that instance

subset.role: Named public files. Raw HDF5 is never committed. Byte SHA-256 after fetch is stored in docs/v06/download_manifest.json, which is not a test score.

from_train_files.assignment: by (file order, trajectory index) before any windowing: first 8 trajectories of each of the three train files are train (24). The next trajectories fill calibration until 64. Leftovers are unused.

splits.from_valid_files: all official valid trajectories of the three in-distribution files are the FNO validation split
splits.from_test_files: all official test trajectories of the three in-distribution files are the in-distribution test split
splits.ood: official valid and test trajectories of Reynolds 1e5, Schmidt 1.0. Those files are never used for training, calibration, or validation.

wsindy.role: solver-free classical baseline: weak-form least-squares coefficient fit, not a support-discovery STLSQ

test_function.center_stride_rationale: Same 1/6 stride as the v0.5.2 fix. 4 * stride / n is not required here (no Kolmogorov k=4), but the stride is reused so the identifier is the repaired WSINDy, not the degenerate v0.5.1 grid.

wsindy.nu_equation: stacked ux and uy: ∫ (u_t + u·∇u + ∇p) φ = nu ∫ u Δφ
wsindy.kappa_equation: tracer: ∫ (s_t + u·∇s) φ = kappa ∫ s Δφ
wsindy.pressure: treated as a known probed field, not a library term

oracle.role: ceiling: the same weak-form fit on the clean full 32 by 64 field, no lattice, no noise

fno_data.role: data-only FNO inverse: the reused FNO2d class maps the trigonometric lift of the noisy lattice to a spatially pooled (log nu, log kappa). It is not a viscosity-conditioned rollout and not a Dedalus search.
fno_data.loss: mean squared error on (log nu, log kappa)
fno_data.checkpoint: lowest validation MSE on the official in-distribution valid split

hybrid.role: FNO-bracket + calibrated split-conformal intervals, adapted from v0.4.1 without a PDE solver. The data-only FNO locates a log-bracket. The WSINDy point is clipped into that bracket. Intervals are split-conformal on the calibration split of 64 instances.
hybrid.score: absolute error in log nu and in log kappa, separately
hybrid.coverage_definition: an instance is covered when true nu and true kappa both lie in their intervals

pysr.reason: PySR needs Julia. The skip is recorded here before scoring.

pass_bars.source: docs roadmap for the first external-dataset inverse; not retuned

nu_kappa_in_dist.name: in_dist_median_rel
nu_kappa_in_dist.statistic: median relative error of the hybrid, mean of the nu median and the kappa median, mean over seeds, in-distribution test, noise 0.01

nu_kappa_ood.name: ood_median_rel
nu_kappa_ood.statistic: same statistic on the OOD slice, noise 0.01

gap.name: ood_over_in_dist
gap.statistic: ood_median_rel / max(in_dist_median_rel, 1e-12) of the hybrid at noise 0.01

coverage.name: interval_coverage
coverage.statistic: hybrid 0.9-interval coverage on in-distribution test at noise 0.01, mean over seeds

hybrid_beats.name: hybrid_beats_baselines_ood
hybrid_beats.statistic: hybrid ood_median_rel at noise 0.01 is strictly less than both wsindy and fno_data on that slice

noise_robustness.name: noise_5pct_not_worse_than_wsindy
noise_robustness.statistic: hybrid in-distribution median rel error at noise 0.05 is <= the wsindy value on the same slice

pass_bars.overall: pass only if every bar above passes

compute.ci: tiny synthetic fixture only. CI never downloads The Well and never trains the study.
